entry.title: Meet the physicist who discovered how to trap light

media:group.media:title: Meet the physicist who discovered how to trap light
media:group.media:description: For four decades, U of T physicist Sajeev John has shaped the field of photonic crystals - structures that can trap and manipulate light. He explains how an idea rooted in theoretical physics has evolved into a field with applications ranging from laser surgery and high-speed communications to solar energy and advanced computing.

entry.title: How photonic crystals could enable flake-thin solar cells

media:group.media:title: How photonic crystals could enable flake-thin solar cells
media:group.media:description: Imagine buildings and automobiles coated in solar cells that generate power wherever sunlight hits. Sajeev John explains how photonic crystals could make this a reality by enabling solar cells that are dramatically thinner and more efficient than today’s designs.
